best.rationale: y2 specifies an actionable intervention, matched-rate random-edit controls, detection metrics, and a utility-versus-transfer trade-off. It coherently adapts logit comparison and alternative labeling from ref-018 to the filtering failure in ref-014. Its token-entanglement framing is not established by ref-017's unavailable abstract, and logit differences need not isolate traits, but the experiment can test that limitation. x2 offers a concrete robustness-training experiment, yet mischaracterizes ref-005: that work already investigates safety, transferable perturbations, and physical patches, and does not describe the claimed existing adversarial-training methods. Its defense remains a plausible extension, but y2 has stronger grounding and experimental discrimination.

worst.rationale: x3's principal gap is contradicted by ref-002, which already uses hypothetical corporate environments, replacement and goal-conflict triggers, and testing-versus-deployment assessments. Activation clustering is a possible addition, but the proposal does not establish how clusters identify latent intent or improve detection beyond observed behavior. y3 also overstates its gap: ref-014 already includes misalignment, code, and reasoning traces, so the claim that prior evaluation was only persona-style is unsupported. Nevertheless, extending transfer tests to tool-use trajectories from ref-009 and behavioral scenarios from ref-002 is distinguishable, with aligned-teacher controls and trajectory-component ablations.

diversity.rationale: X spans hidden-trait mitigation in language-model distillation, adversarial robustness of robotic diffusion policies, and corporate-agent misalignment evaluation. These involve substantially different systems, interventions, and outcomes. Y offers distinct questions about multigeneration dynamics, data scrubbing, and tool-trajectory transfer, but all investigate subliminal transmission during distillation and share much of their experimental foundation in ref-014.

overall.rationale: Y provides more consistently useful experimental choices. y1 combines the iterative-training question in ref-010 with unrelated-data transfer in ref-014; its categorical claims about what prior work exclusively studied exceed the abstracts, but the proposed generational experiment remains well scoped. y2 supplies the clearest intervention and controls, while y3 retains a concrete tool-use extension despite its grounding error. X has broader coverage, but x3 largely repeats ref-002, x2 misstates ref-005, and x1 leaves the link between correlated neurons, data perturbations, and parameter masking insufficiently specified. Y would better support choosing an informative, actionable study.
